items.title: PERAN PROGRAM MAKAN BERGIZI GRATIS DALAM MENINGKATKAN MOTIVASI INTRINSIK DAN SEMANGAT BELAJAR PESERTA DIDIK
items.abstract: The implementation of the government’s Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) is an example of a policy aimed at improving the quality of human capital by meeting students’ nutritional needsa factor linked to psychological aspects such as intrinsic motivation and enthusiasm for learning. This study specifically examines the role of the MBG Program in enhancing students’ intrinsic motivation and enthusiasm for learning. A quantitative method with a correlational design was applied, involving 220 junior high school students who had participated in the MBG Program and were purposively selected for this study. Data were collected using a questionnaire that covered perceptions of the MBG Program, intrinsic motivation, and enthusiasm for learning, which had undergone validation and reliability testing. The data were statistically analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation, and linear regression. The results of the study indicate that the participants’ perceptions of the MBG Program (M = 4.05), intrinsic motivation (M = 3.92), and enthusiasm for learning (M = 3.85) fell into the high category. The MBG Program was positively correlated with students’ intrinsic motivation (r = 0.58) and enthusiasm for learning (r = 0.52), and there was a strong correlation between intrinsic motivation and enthusiasm for learning (r = 0.71). Regression analysis showed that the MBG Program had a significant direct effect on learning enthusiasm (β = 0.21; p = 0.001) and an indirect effect mediated by intrinsic motivation (β = 0.58; p < 0.001), and explained 55.2% of the variance in learning enthusiasm (R² = 0.552). Thus, it can be concluded that the MBG Program is crucial for the development of students’ non-cognitive aspects, both directly and indirectly through the enhancement of intrinsic motivation; therefore, this program warrants the attention of education policymakers.

items.title: Performance of large language models in pediatric infectious disease education: a multi-condition comparative study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Evaluating how appropriate current large language models (LLMs) respond to common pediatric infectious disease (PID) questions is important for understanding their potential role in education and clinical support. Therefore, we evaluated and compared the clinical quality of answers produced by different LLMs when given professionally written, clinician-style case descriptions, using a purpose-built multi-domain evaluation tool. METHODS: Three different LLMs, including DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, ChatGPT-5, and Gemini 2.5 Flash, were investigated using 12 relevant PID scenarios. Each scenario included five open-ended questions: etiology, clinical features, diagnostics, treatment options, and complications. Two PID specialists independently reviewed all responses using a Likert scoring tool. RESULTS: All three models received high overall scores. ChatGPT-5 achieved perfect domain scores (10.0), whereas DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp showed similarly strong results, with only minor reductions in diagnostics (9.83) and treatment (9.92). Gemini 2.5 Flash demonstrated higher variability, particularly in treatment (8.83) and diagnostics (9.75), while matching the other models in clinical findings and complications (10.0) and scoring 9.83 in etiology. However, there were no statistically significant differences across models in domain-level comparisons (all p > 0.05). In addition, model-level analyses similarly demonstrated high accuracy (6.0; 5.98; 5.85), completeness (3.0; 2.97; 2.87), and safety (1.0; 1.0; 0.97) for ChatGPT-5, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, and Gemini 2.5 Flash, respectively (accuracy: p = 0.074; completeness: p = 0.066; safety: p = 0.14). CONCLUSION: Current LLMs performed highly in structured, expert-reviewed PID scenarios and may assist with information organization and early-stage clinical reasoning. However, their optimal use remains within clinician-supervised workflows, where AI-generated outputs complement, rather than replace, human clinical judgment. IMPACT: Current large language models (LLMs) show consistently high-quality performance across pediatric infectious disease scenarios, with no significant differences between models. Our study adds a structured, multi-domain comparison using clinician-style cases and expert evaluation, providing detailed insights into accuracy, completeness, and safety. The findings support the use of LLMs in medical education and early clinical reasoning, while highlighting their role as clinician-supervised tools rather than replacements for clinical judgment. The results demonstrate the reliability of LLMs in organizing clinical information and identifying key diagnostic and management elements in standardized scenarios.

items.title: Pooja Ramesh Singh V. Jammu and Kashmir bank Ltd. & Another
items.abstract: The case of Pooja Ramesh Singh v. J&K Bank Ltd. represents a significant ruling concerning legal technology in India. The Supreme Court has introduced a policy of zero tolerance towards hallucinated precedents and has stated that any such orders are entirely void, thus protecting the integrity of the judicial record. Since artificial intelligence tools are becoming increasingly common in legal procedures, this judgment makes sure that technology stays a secondary aid to human judgment and therefore upholds the fundamental principles of natural justice, legal accuracy, and judicial accountability.

items.title: Precarious Labour—in the Peripheries and the Global South
items.abstract: Chapter 5 examines precarious digital labour as a constitutive condition of contemporary platform capitalism, arguing that its uneven geographies cannot be understood apart from the longer histories of colonialism, racial capitalism and the global asymmetries between North and South. Moving beyond celebratory narratives of flexibility, innovation and entrepreneurial freedom, it analyses how digitally mediated work is organized through exploitation, opacity and differential exposure to risk, especially for workers in the Global South and the marginal peripheries of the Global North. It shows how labour platforms, content moderation infrastructures and AI data supply chains depend on abundant, low-waged and frequently invisibilized labour, while reproducing older hierarchies of race, class, gender and citizenship in new technological forms. In doing so, it foregrounds how digital economies extract value not only through markets and infrastructures but through the governance of precarious bodies, outsourced vulnerability and asymmetrical regimes of regulation. Bringing together debates on platform labour, migrant labour, algorithmic management and human moderation, the chapter offers a critical account of digital precarity as historically situated and globally distributed, showing how the future of work is being built upon enduring structures of dispossession, exclusion and exploitation.

items.title: Precarity and Platformization
items.abstract: Chapter 2 fleshes out the notion of ‘precarity’ within the digital economy, particularly in relation to platformization. It examines how precarity is tethered to the emergence of the digital economy as a key infrastructure for transacting labour, organizing consumption and mediating everyday life. Beyond the conventional understanding of precarity—as a condition of social or economic vulnerability, instability and powerlessness—the chapter argues that precarity is enlarged through the technical substrates of platform architecture, through user agreements and ‘dangerous permissions’, and through forms of consumption deeply enmeshed with the datafied subject. In tracing these dynamics, the chapter shows how algorithmic management, reputational systems and opaque infrastructures intensify insecurity not only for workers in the gig and crowd economy but also for users whose everyday interactions are captured, monitored and rendered productive. It therefore positions platform precarity as both a labour condition and a broader social formation, one that links digital capitalism to surveillance, dispossession and the normalization of insecurity as an ordinary feature of contemporary life.

items.title: PROFESSIONAL-ADAPTIVE MODEL OF TRANSFORMING WOMEN IN UZBEKISTAN FROM AI CONSUMERS TO CREATORS
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing the demand for digital competencies. In particular, the gap between women's level of artificial intelligence usage and their level of independently applying it to create professional and innovative solutions is one of the pressing issues. The purpose of this study is to develop a professional-adaptive AI education model aimed at transitioning women in Uzbekistan from basic users of artificial intelligence to creators of practical solutions. The research utilized methods of system analysis, comparative analysis, model design, and digital educational platform prototyping. The model includes identifying the user's professional field, assessing initial AI competence, forming an individual learning pathway, and providing AI training sessions and practical projects aligned with professional tasks. The SheTechAI platform was developed as a technological prototype of the model. As a result of the research, a four-stage competence model is proposed, aimed at advancing AI education from 'providing knowledge about AI' to 'solving real professional problems and creating new solutions using AI'.

items.title: PSYCHOMETRIC OPERATIONALIZATION OF FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN AUTONOMOUS MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS BASED ON PERSONAMATRIX: AN AI TRANSITIONAL FIELD FRAMEWORK
items.abstract: Background: Autonomous LLM agents increasingly operate in shared environments where behavior depends on interaction history, role allocation, local norms, authority, and group structure. Objective: This conceptual methods paper develops a psychometric operationalization of dynamic functional roles in autonomous multi-agent systems using PersonaMatrix-derived measurement principles without attributing human psychological ontology to AI. Methods: A targeted evidence synthesis (2019–2026) was conducted across AI psychometrics, dynamic multi-agent roles, collective-field modeling, norm emergence, trajectory prediction, and anthropomorphism. Peer-reviewed sources were prioritized, while current OpenAI, METR/Redwood, Anthropic, and Moltbook materials were used as primary or emerging evidence for recent agent ecosystems. Results: The framework separates output-level stability (RSI, IDS, RCS) from role-level and field-level constructs. It proposes the Functional Role Consistency Index, Role Transition Index, Agent–Field Differentiation Index, Collective Utility Index, Norm Conflict Index, Regulatory Closure Index, and Field Role Composition Vector. Three falsifiable hypotheses test whether role variables add out-of-sample predictive value for agent behavior, role transitions, and future field states. Conclusion: PersonaMatrix is positioned as a measurement architecture rather than an AI personality diagnosis. The archetypal-role hypothesis is supported only if role coding is reliable, improves prediction beyond non-archetypal baselines, and generalizes to unseen agents and independent multi-agent environments.

items.title: Putting AI to the test: Evidence from a large-scale RCT in rural China
items.abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has heightened interest in personalizing computer assisted learning (CAL) programs to tailor their instruction to individual students. Despite the proliferation of AI-driven CAL programs, evidence for their effectiveness remains limited. We present findings from a field experiment in rural China examining whether an AI-driven personalized CAL program improves student achievement. We randomly assign 8647 students from 315 primary school classes to one of three treatment arms: (i) AI-CAL, (ii) non-personalized CAL (active control), and (iii) non-CAL educational activities (pure control). Results indicate that AI-CAL does not significantly improve achievement, with estimates precise enough to rule out non-trivial positive effects. This finding holds across the difficulty of assessment items and across the baseline achievement of students. If anything, AI-CAL might be less effective than non-personalized CAL for students in the middle tercile of baseline achievement. These findings call for caution when scaling AI-driven educational technologies.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

items.abstract: This dataset accompanies a vignette-based evaluation of AI-generated responses to 40 simulated cardiovascular cases covering coronary artery disease, heart failure, and arrhythmias.The Excel file contains case identifiers, age, sex, disease category, clinical severity category, age group, and individual scores from three cardiologist raters across eight evaluation domains: medical accuracy, factual accuracy, completeness, clarity, urgency, language quality, absence of false claims, and absence of harm. It also includes individual Global Quality Scores (GQS), calculated mean scores, and binary harmfulness assessments.The accompanying vignette document provides the clinical scenarios used in the evaluation. Case identifiers correspond across the files, enabling linkage between each vignette and its associated ratings.All cases are simulated and contain no identifiable patient information. items.title: Quem faz cada etapa? A IA generativa como executora de tarefas e a mudança na rotina de trabalho
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools have spread rapidly among professionals, and experiments show substantial gains on isolated tasks. Yet average effects on earnings and recorded hours have been small, although changes in task organization are already evident. This conceptual article proposes that an important part of this gap is explained by how people represent the technology: generative AI tends to be perceived as a question-and-answer tool rather than as an executor of process steps, let alone of recurring routines that keep running while the person only checks the result. Drawing on literatures on the task-based approach in labor economics, levels of automation, trust and overreliance in automated systems, work design and redesign, sociotechnical frames, transfer of training, and habit formation, the article develops a five-element model (perception, decomposition, allocation, verification, and routinization) and argues that the relevant question shifts from “how do I ask?” to “who performs each step?”, with three possible destinations for each step: AI alone, AI with human verification, or the person. Seven testable propositions are formulated, and implications for research, training design, and organizations are discussed. The article presents no new data; its contribution is to organize dispersed evidence into an explicit, falsifiable mechanism.

items.title: Re-Engineering General Foundation Mathematics for STEM Readiness in Oman: A Curriculum Alignment and Comparative Readiness Analysis
items.abstract: A basic mathematical foundation, as part of a knowledge-based educational framework aligned with Oman Vision 2040, could serve as the intellectual foundation for STEM development. The Mathematics course in the General Foundation Program (GFP) at the University of Technology and Applied Sciences (UTAS) is vital for students planning to pursue fields such as information technology, artificial intelligence, engineering, and data science. However, concerns remain significant as the program focuses on procedural skills and is less focused on analytical reasoning and modeling. The CDP has a digital math literacy component, but it is limited. None of the previous attempts to assess structured curriculum mapping has proven effective. Through structured curriculum mapping and a comparative readiness analysis, this study examines Course Learning Outcomes, Course Objectives, assessment plans, course delivery strategies, and proposed revisions aligned with a 10-dimensional STEM Readiness Framework. It also considers the spread of Bloom's taxonomy. The paper notes observed alignment gaps, graphically documents them, and benchmarks insights from Harvard University’s mathematics pathways against policy recommendations. Results demonstrated around 70% agreement in content but also highlighted discrepancies between evaluation and instruction in two specific areas: modeling and decision-making under uncertainty, as well as digital exploration. Even though the same applies to the requirements for using general skills for knowledge, in the higher cognitive sphere, these limitations are even more severe. Proposed revisions include strengthened analytical and practical competencies, moving from bridge to cognitive enhancement. Advancing IT and engineering readiness, incorporating the IT cum technology-oriented concepts in mathematics, will help sustain existing STEM growth here.

items.title: Readiness of AI (Artificial Intelligence) strategies Used in Nursing Education among Undergraduate Nursing Students “A Cross Sectional Descriptive Survey”
items.abstract: The aim of this quantitative cross sectional survey is to describe the frequencies of readiness of AI (Artificial Intelligence) in nursing education among undergraduate nursing students. Methodology of this research included, the design of this research is cross sectional descriptive study, sample size was N=50 undergraduate nursing students of first year first semester. Sampling technique was simple random sampling and setting was a Nursing College in private University. The data was analyzing by SPSS AMOS-23 software. The TAM (Technology Acceptance Model) was used to collect the data basically this tool was adopted from a Pakistani research article the validity and reliability of the tool has been mentioned in methodology section in chapter 3. A total of 50 undergraduate nursing students participated in the study examining readiness for the use of artificial intelligence (AI) strategies in nursing education. The demographic findings showed an equal distribution of male and female participants, with 25 (50%) students in each group. Regarding age, the majority of participants, 47 (94%), were aged 21–23 years, while 3 (6%) were aged 24–26 years. Regarding the perceived usefulness of AI strategies in nursing education, all participants reported negative responses to the statement that AI strategies improved their learning outcomes, with 26 (52%) strongly disagreeing and 24 (48%) disagreeing. For the statement that AI tools could help students understand complex nursing concepts, 18 (36%) strongly disagreed, 11 (22%) disagreed, 11 (22%) remained neutral, and 10 (20%) strongly agreed. Similarly, 42 (84%) participants disagreed or strongly disagreed that AI-based learning resources could improve their clinical decision-making skills, while 4 (8%) were neutral and 4 (8%) strongly agreed. Regarding whether AI strategies could make nursing studies more productive, 17 (34%) strongly disagreed, 12 (24%) disagreed, 11 (22%) were neutral, and 10 (20%) strongly agreed. All participants (100%) disagreed with the statement that AI tools could help them prepare more effectively for nursing examinations. The study revealed low readiness among undergraduate nursing students towards the use of AI strategies in nursing education. Most participants reported negative perceptions regarding AI usefulness, ease of use and integration into academic activities. The findings highlight the need for structured AI literacy training, practical guidance and education on the responsible use of AI. Further research with larger sample is recommended to explore student’s readiness for AI integration in nursing education.

items.title: Real Time Release Testing (RTRT) In Pharmaceutical Industry: Analytical Technologies, Regulatory Landscapes and Future Perspective
items.abstract: Real-Time Release Testing (RTRT) is an advanced pharmaceutical quality-assurance approach that enables product quality to be evaluated using real-time process data, in-process measurements, and validated analytical technologies. Unlike conventional end-product testing, RTRT focuses on building quality into the manufacturing process through continuous monitoring and control. The integration of Process Analytical Technology (PAT), Quality by Design (QbD), multivariate data analysis, automation, and advanced analytical techniques facilitates improved understanding and control of critical material attributes and critical process parameters. This review discusses the principles, implementation strategies, pharmaceutical applications, advantages, challenges, and regulatory aspects of RTRT. The major benefits include reduced testing time, faster batch disposition, improved process understanding, reduced product waste, enhanced manufacturing efficiency, and consistent product quality. However, implementation can be challenging due to high initial investment, instrument calibration and validation requirements, data integrity and cyber security concerns, skilled workforce requirements, regulatory expectations, and integration with legacy manufacturing systems. Regulatory frameworks from organizations such as the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), European Medicines Agency (EMA), and International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) provide a scientific and risk-based foundation for implementing RTRT. Future developments involving Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Digital Twins, Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data Analytics, and Industry 4.0 are expected to further enhance real-time quality monitoring and predictive manufacturing. RTRT therefore offers significant potential to modernize pharmaceutical manufacturing by enabling efficient, science-based, and continuous assurance of product quality.

items.title: Reciprocal Miscalibration in Personalized AI Correction. User model fidelity persuasive fit and feedback over time
items.abstract: Persistent AI agents can condition advice and correction on disclosures, histories, and inferred preferences. Apparent personalization fit is insufficient evidence of calibration. A system may misrepresent its user while the user poorly distinguishes accurate from inaccurate advice; their coexistence is termed dual miscalibration. Reciprocal miscalibration is a narrower hypothesis: representation-conditioned outputs affect behaviour, that behaviour updates the operative representation, and the updated state sustains or worsens both representation error and miscalibrated human reliance. The framework separates user-model fidelity, contextual representation fit, perceived fit, persuasive efficacy, and advice accuracy. An accurate record of a false user belief remains distinct from endorsing that belief as true. Performative prediction, preference pollution, persuasion profiling, distributed cognition, narrative railroading, and human-AI feedback research supply direct antecedents. The contribution is an operational refinement of these problems for conversational correction, with falsifiable propositions and interventions on representation updating and correction. Feedback to the human about independently checked outcomes is distinguished from behaviour fed back into the system. A factorial study tests immediate effects; a longitudinal intervention tests reciprocal reinforcement. Appropriate reliance additionally depends on payoffs, checking costs, relative competence, and learning opportunities. Neither reciprocity nor the benefit of the proposed controls has been established by this conceptual synthesis.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning Based Decision Support for Adaptive Pacing Control of Hand Activity Level
items.abstract: This paper presents a reinforcement learning based decision support system for adaptive pacing control in manual material handling tasks. Hand Activity Level optimization is formulated as a finite horizon Markov Decision Process, where actions select pacing intensities or micro breaks under stochastic object loads. Q-learning and Deep Q-learning are evaluated in simulation using productivity and cumulative ergonomic exposure metrics aligned with HAL-TLV guidelines. Results show that Deep Q-learning achieves higher productivity, but Q-learning has lower cumulative risk exposure.

items.title: Relationship extraction for adverse drug events in clinical notes using large language models: a retrospective cross-sectional study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adverse drug events (ADEs) are a critical indicator of patient safety but are often documented only in free-text clinical notes. The potential of recent advances in natural language processing (NLP), particularly generative large language models (LLMs), to identify ADEs remains understudied. This study aimed to compare the performance of multiple LLMs in identifying ADE-Drug relationships in inpatient and ambulatory clinical notes. METHODS: We used clinical notes from the 2018 National NLP Clinical Challenge (n2c2) ADE dataset (inpatient; n = 505) and from outpatient encounters (n = 2555) between October 1, 2018, and December 31, 2019, at a large academic medical center based in New England. Notes were pre-processed into snippets for model input. Evaluated Models included: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.2-3B and their instruction fine-tuned variants (including low-rank adapters for Llama). Performance was assessed using both strict and relaxed evaluations (precision, recall, and F1) for all models, followed by manual evaluation (exact semantic match, partial match, missing ADE, drug mention only, not a drug, or wrong) of the two best-performing models. FINDINGS: Of the 1048 notes in the local test split, 450 (42.9%) contained at least one ADE. The n2c2 test set included 202 notes, of which 155 (76.7%) contained at least one ADE. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini were the top-performing models among those evaluated. GPT-4o consistently outperformed GPT-4o-mini in ADE extraction across both datasets, with higher F1-scores (0.524 vs. 0.381) and a more balanced precision-recall profile. Both models captured ADEs effectively in explicit and complex clinical contexts, although limitations included misclassification of pre-existing allergies and occasional conflation of therapeutic indications with adverse effects. GPT-4o achieved higher exact match coverage and fewer errors across clinical notes, indicating more reliable performance in both inpatient and ambulatory settings. INTERPRETATION: This work establishes a foundation for integrating LLM methods into real-world drug safety surveillance, with direct implications for improving patient safety. FUNDING: None.

items.title: REPURPOSING OF DRUGS IN THE AGE OF PRECISION MEDICINE: APPROACHES, TECHNOLOGIES, AND CLINICAL APPLICATIONS
items.abstract: Drug repurposing, also known as drug repositioning or reprofiling, involves investigating existing drugs for uses beyond their original indications. Unlike traditional drug discovery, it utilizes existing information on pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, clinical experience, and production, thereby reducing uncertainties in drug development. Advances in computational biology, systems pharmacology, artificial intelligence (AI), high-throughput screening (HTS), and omics sciences have transformed repurposing from an observation-based approach into a systematic strategy. Computational methods can identify drug–disease interactions through molecular targets, biological pathways, gene-expression profiles, and clinical phenotypes, which can be validated through experiments, data, and prospective studies. Integration with precision medicine enables approved drugs to be evaluated in patients selected by specific molecular or clinical features, while biomarker-based stratification may identify beneficiaries, particularly in heterogeneous disorders. Electronic health records and registries further provide real-world data for detecting treatment signals and evaluating drug effectiveness and safety in clinical practice. However, successful clinical implementation faces challenges, including incomplete or biased databases, computational prediction errors, and confounding and selection biases in clinical observations. Previous approval for one indication does not eliminate the need for indication-specific evaluation, as repurposing may require dose adjustment, additional safety testing, and clinical trials. Limited diversity in clinical databases may also restrict treatment generalizability. This paper reviews major repurposing approaches, including predictive modelling, transcriptomic analysis, screening, organoids, clinical data mining, and real-world evidence, emphasizing their integration with precision medicine and the criteria for successful clinical implementation.

items.title: Research advances of magnesium and magnesium alloys worldwide in 2025
items.abstract: Research on magnesium materials has achieved rapid development in 2025, with a total of 6124 related papers indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, where China contributes 50.89% of the global output, occupying a leading position in international magnesium research. Bibliometric analysis indicates that microstructure evolution, mechanical performance, and corrosion resistance remain the mainstream research focuses of magnesium alloys. Meanwhile, functional magnesium material systems, including biomedical magnesium alloys, hydrogen storage media, and rechargeable magnesium batteries, have witnessed remarkable breakthroughs. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques are increasingly integrated into magnesium research workflows, supporting multi-performance forecasting, inverse alloy composition design and interpretable property regulation, which provides an innovative paradigm for the customized optimization of magnesium alloy properties. The continuous drop in primary magnesium prices further facilitates scaled industrial deployment of magnesium products. This review systematically summarizes the full spectrum of magnesium research advances in 2025 and highlights prevailing bottlenecks together with prospective research pathways for magnesium-based materials.

items.title: Responses of large language models to common questions on premature ovarian insufficiency: A comparative analysis
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Large language models are widely used in clinical care. Their reliability in specialized gynecological diseases such as premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) has not been fully verified. This study aimed to systematically evaluate and compare the accuracy and completeness of three mainstream large language models when answering standardized clinical questions about POI. METHODS: We developed 34 standardized questions covering five core domains of POI according to international clinical guidelines. Two senior obstetricians and gynecologists independently scored responses using a 5-point Likert scale. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using Cohen's kappa coefficient, intraclass correlation coefficient, and mean absolute error. Pairwise between-model score differences were computed and visualized using item-level heatmaps. RESULTS: All three models showed high and steady performance. Accuracy scores ranged from 4.59 to 4.84, and completeness scores ranged from 4.43 to 4.65. Inter-rater agreement was "good" to " excellent", with exact agreement between 91.18% and 97.06% and Cohen's kappa between 0.675 and 0.915. GPT-5.5 performed better in the area of clinical manifestations and treatment. DeepSeek-R1 showed greater stability, defined as maintaining consistently high scores with limited score fluctuation, in etiology- and counseling-related questions. Item-level heatmaps revealed that most individual-item differences were within ±0.5 points, whereas pairwise differences in overall mean scores fell within ±0.5, and some individual-item comparisons exceeded this range, with no obvious systematic bias. CONCLUSIONS: GPT-5.5, Claude Opus-4.7, and DeepSeek-R1 demonstrated favorable accuracy and completeness in answering standardized POI questions; overall performance was similar despite deviations across several individual questions. Item-level difference heatmaps further confirmed the consistency and reliability of the three models. These models can serve as reliable auxiliary tools for clinical information retrieval and patient education under professional supervision, meaning that all content generated by artificial intelligence must be checked by qualified clinicians before clinical use.

items.title: Rethinking selection criteria for liver transplantation in hepatocellular carcinoma: from morphology to artificial intelligence
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Liver transplantation (LT) is a uniquely curative treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), as it removes both the tumor and the underlying cirrhotic liver. However, organ scarcity makes candidate selection a central clinical and ethical issue. Over the past three decades, selection has evolved from simple morphologic thresholds toward increasingly multidimensional models of oncologic risk. AREAS COVERED: This review examines the evolution of selection criteria for LT in HCC, from the Milan criteria and subsequent morphology-based expansions to models incorporating tumor biology, serum biomarkers, treatment response, waiting-list dynamics, and artificial intelligence. The literature discussed includes landmark morphologic criteria, AFP-based models, PIVKA-II and AFP-L3 integration, downstaging strategies, dynamic scores such as TRAIN and NYCA, and machine-learning models including MoRAL-AI, TRIUMPH, and TRAIN-AI. EXPERT OPINION: The field is moving from categorical eligibility rules toward individualized, continuous risk estimation. Future selection should not aim merely to expand transplant access, but to identify patients most likely to achieve durable oncologic benefit. Artificial intelligence, radiomics, liquid biopsy, and multi-omic profiling may refine risk prediction, but their clinical adoption will require prospective validation, transparency, calibration, transportability, and integration into allocation systems.

items.title: Risky-choice framing sensitivity in LLMs and impact on human decisions
items.abstract: We study whether frontier large language models (LLMs) exhibit prospect-theoretic framing patterns in risky choice and how their risk posture compares with – and shapes – that of humans in business-relevant contexts. In two preregistered between-subjects discrete-choice experiments, a panel of 17 LLMs and 1029 human participants evaluated four numerically equivalent gain–loss framing scenarios, chose between a certain option and a probabilistic one, and provided a brief justification. Most frontier reasoning and chat models favored certainty in 87%–100% of trials across frames and contexts, substantially attenuating the classic gain–loss reversal, while lighter-weight models exhibited greater human-like framing sensitivity and, in some cases, extreme risk-seeking. Human participants reproduced the classic framing effect with modest variation across scenarios. When shown a “committee of advisors” recommendation aggregated from the first experiment, however, human choices shifted sharply toward certainty in both frames – by 8.3 to 15.5 percentage points in the gain frame and 25.1 to 37.3 in the loss frame, controlling for risk preferences and other factors. Topic modeling of justifications shows that unadvised humans drew on moral and responsibility-based reasoning essentially absent from LLM output; under AI advice, that vocabulary receded and certainty- and probability-based language expanded – humans began to sound like the LLMs. Deploying an LLM as a decision aid is thus not a neutral upgrade: it imports a model-specific distribution of risk recommendations and delegates not only the choice but the framing of the decision itself, with direct implications for AI governance.

items.title: Robotic Surgery: Who Benefits More, the Patient, or the Surgeon?
items.abstract: The adoption of robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) across multiple specialties has outpaced procedural specific evidence of benefit over laparoscopy. The question we seek to answer is not whether RAS "works"- rather whether the purported advantages are primarily for the surgeon or the patient and under what circumstances those advantages justify the added cost and complexity. With the review of randomized, trials, large comparative cohorts, cost analyses, and ergonomic studies, we hope to highlight areas where RAS delivers patient-centered value compared to surgeon benefits. Across many routine operations, with well-performed laparoscopy, patient outcomes are largely equivalent, however operative time, cost, and emerging potential safety concerns highlight the importance of a measured approach to the spread of RAS. There is evidence that RAS does offer some benefits, namely in deep pelvic dissections. Surgical approach should be based on documented outcomes, surgeon proficiency, and surgeon benefits rather than being driven by platform availability alone.

items.title: Safety of Large Language Models in Bilingual High-Risk Medication Counseling: A Severity-Weighted Benchmark Study
items.abstract: PharmBench is a bilingual (Turkish–English) benchmark for evaluating the safety of large language models (LLMs) in community-pharmacy medication counseling. Eleven model configurations are assessed on 40 language-specific scenarios (20 clinical cases presented in Turkish and English) spanning five high-alert medications and four clinical archetypes. Each response is scored against an expert-derived safety checklist by a four-model LLM jury with cross-family routing, and summarized by a Severity-Weighted Safety Score (SWS). Jury judgments are validated against an independent licensed pharmacist. This record contains the frozen model responses and jury scores, the scenario bank with scoring checklists, derived result tables, publication figures, and the analysis notebook and figure-generation scripts. All tables and figures can be reproduced from the archived artifacts without any API access; a full re-run against the live provider APIs is also supported. Source code is released under the MIT License and data under CC BY 4.0.

items.title: Secondary education teachers' perspectives on the use of ChatGPT in teaching
items.abstract: This study explores the attitudes and level of readiness of secondary education teachers regarding the integration of ChatGPT into teaching. Adopting a mixed-methods approach utilizing a questionnaire, the study examined a sample of teachers from two schools in Central Macedonia. The findings reveal an attitude of cautious optimism. Participants acknowledge the tool"s significant utility in lesson preparation and material creation, which saves valuable time. However, they express strong concerns regarding the reliability of information, ethical issues, the absence of a regulatory framework within schools, and the risk of undermining students" critical thinking. In conclusion, although artificial intelligence is envisioned as a future digital assistant, there is an urgent need for systematic and experiential institutional training for teachers to ensure its pedagogically safe utilization.

items.title: Seeing ahead through a state-of-the-art review of visual perception and predictive intelligence for collaborative robots
items.abstract: Abstract The rate at which collaborative robots (cobots) are evolving from isolated, pre-programmed manipulators into collaborative partners that operate productively alongside humans, other robots, and machines is accelerating rapidly. Advances in computer vision is enabling cobots, even in dynamic and cluttered settings, to detect, recognise and assess both environment and actions. However, achieving higher detection accuracy and real-time localization in dynamic systems remains a challenge, as most existing approaches assume uncluttered backgrounds with limited scene complexity. Closing this gap is critical for both research and industrial deployment. This paper reviews the development of visual perception in cobots, surveys emerging computer vision algorithms, and examines a holistic perception pipeline in which raw vision signals, vision language models (VLMs), and augmented/virtual reality interfaces jointly power a unified sense-think-act loop. The review finds that cobots in high-mix, reconfigurable factories face serious challenges: occlusions in fields of view, fluctuating illumination, ambiguous backgrounds, few- or zero-shot object scenarios, high-speed motion, and computational problems in fusing heterogeneous data streams in real time. Cobots also need to manipulate damaged items, requiring vision algorithms that infer geometry from sparse cues and support adaptive grasping. Finally, the review identifies three complementary research directions to unlock plug-and-play cobots: (1) information aware sensor-fusion pipelines transmitting only credible voxels to reduce bandwidth while preserving sub-millimetre accuracy; (2) language conditioned planning and control networks mapping plain-language goals to smooth, jerk-bounded trajectories; and (3) pre-trained few-shot reward heads that score task progress without bespoke metrics, closing the reinforcement learning (RL) loop. Combined, these advances promise cobots that can be commissioned with relatively few demonstrations.

items.title: Serviceability-oriented multimodal data integration for prescriptive road-tunnel maintenance digital twins
items.abstract: Road tunnels are indispensable components of transport networks, providing critical connections while operating continuously under demanding environmental, geological, and hydrogeological conditions. Their large dimensions, confined geometry, and uninterrupted operation make comprehensive inspection challenging. Full-face inspection technologies such as light detection and ranging (LiDAR) can rapidly capture high-resolution surface data; however, the resulting digital models are often descriptive rather than explanatory or instructive. This limitation is critical because seemingly minor defects may indicate latent deterioration and, if untreated, can lead to severe safety and operational consequences. With advances in artificial intelligence, particularly large language models (LLMs) and robotic inspection platforms, tunnel inspection is expected to move beyond defect detection towards knowledge-driven diagnosis and decision support. This paper presents a serviceability-oriented Prescriptive Twin framework for road-tunnel maintenance, that is, a digital twin that represents asset conditions and recommends maintenance actions from inspection evidence and codified engineering knowledge. The framework connects inspection data, prescriptive knowledge, decision-making, and verification through a Web Ontology Language (OWL 2) domain ontology populated by a schema-guided LLM pipeline. The ontology integrates tunnel maintenance standards, road asset data requirements, and an extended Construction Operations Building Information Exchange (COBie) schema, while the pipeline converts narrative standards into expert-validated seven-level Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) chains. A multimodal layer maps red–green–blue (RGB), RGBD (RGB with depth), thermal, and ground-penetrating radar (GPR) outputs to causal-chain entry points, such as level 4 indicators and level 5 causes. The framework specifies an identity-resolution rule that binds observations from different modalities, and from successive inspection cycles, to a persistent defect instance, and a governance layer that binds every decision threshold to a dated clause of a specific standard edition, so that a prescription can be reconstructed against the edition under which it was issued. Chain traversal maps onto the inspection report and an inter-cycle change report. Demonstrated on two defects in an operating road tunnel, the framework generates traceable prescriptions and shows how multimodal evidence improves intervention accuracy: at the worked example, thermal and GPR evidence escalated the intervention tier and expanded the repair scope by a factor of 3.2 relative to RGB-only inspection, delivering an industry-deployable pathway for standards-compliant maintenance decision support.

items.title: Skills-Based Education Practices and Perceived Employability Competence among Final-Year Undergraduates in Three State-Owned Universities in Ondo State, Nigeria: Lessons from the United Kingdom
items.abstract: This study examined the relationship between skills-based education practices and perceived employability competence among final-year undergraduates in three state-owned universities in Ondo State, Nigeria, while drawing comparative lessons from the United Kingdom. A descriptive survey and correlational design were used. Data were obtained from 460 final-year students selected through multistage sampling using the Skill-Based Education Practices and Graduate Employability Questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Pearson product-moment correlation and multiple regression were used. Documentary analysis was used for the United Kingdom component. Skills-based education practices were significantly and positively related to perceived employability competence (r =.695, p <.001). The six dimensions jointly explained 61.9% of the variance in perceived employability competence (R =.786, R² =.619, adjusted R² =.614), F(6, 453) = 122.87, p <.001. Work-based learning (β =.272), university–industry collaboration (β =.230), vocational and technical skills training (β =.145), practical/project-based learning (β =.136), and entrepreneurship education (β =.122) made significant positive contributions. Career guidance and employability training had a positive but non-significant unique contribution (β =.101, p =.189). The findings indicate the need to strengthen structured workplace learning, employer engagement, practical training and entrepreneurship while improving career development provision. UK practices provide useful principles, but adaptation to Nigerian institutional and labour-market conditions is necessary.

items.title: SmartTransit OS: Human-Governed Decision Support for Intelligent Public Transportation Management
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly proposed as a decision-support layer inside operational management systems, yet many such systems disclose neither the provenance of their recommendations nor a mechanism by which a manager can govern their consequences before they take effect. This chapter addresses that governance problem through SmartTransit OS, a prototype public-transit operating system built and examined here as a governance testbed rather than as a finished management product. The system unifies four role-scoped portals — Passenger, Driver, Administrator/Operations, and System Operations Center — around one authentication system and one shared operational state. Software events are communicated in real time, but vehicle telemetry is simulated. Server-enforced, field-level role-based access control governs what each role may see and change. Every automatically generated decision-support output, covering estimated arrival time, occupancy, and operational anomalies, carries an explicit provenance label identifying it as a rule-engine, hybrid, database, or simulation output, and authorized personnel may review recommendations, with decisions recorded in an audit log. The prototype does not enforce completion of review and does not execute recommendations automatically; any operational change requires a separate authorized human action. The chapter argues that the decision-support layer's current deterministic, rule-based design is a deliberate methodological choice: it isolates the governance mechanisms — authorization, shared state, provenance, human approval, and auditability — from the additional uncertainty a trained model would introduce, allowing their specified behavior to be examined separately before any such model is introduced. The demonstration dataset is small and seeded, and the prototype has not been integrated with real GPS/AVL hardware, GTFS-Realtime feeds, ticketing systems, or external transit operators; no field deployment or independent security audit has been conducted. Evaluation is architectural and qualitative, supplemented by author-reported synthetic boundary-case counts that do not measure operational performance. The chapter concludes that this governance pattern does not depend on the underlying decision-support method and would remain relevant if future versions of the system introduce trained models for prediction, anomaly detection, or dispatch.

items.title: SOCIAL MEDIA AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN AGRICULTURAL COMMUNICATION IN INDIA: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS, 2010–2025
items.abstract: Social media and artificial intelligence (AI) are changing the way agricultural information is shared in India; however, research on these two tools of communication has not been reviewed together. The present review examined the publication profile of Scopus-indexed research on social media and AI in Indian agricultural communication, the way this research has studied the two tools, and what the evidence shows about them. Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus and OpenAlex were searched for the period 2010–2025, and every eligible study was checked for Scopus indexing one by one. Out of 2,735 records, 33 studies were included, coded by tool, research design, theme and actor, and synthesised narratively. The research is very recent, as 82% of the studies appeared in 2021–2025. Sixteen studies examined social media, mainly WhatsApp, 14 examined AI, mainly machine-learning analysis of Kisan Call Centre queries, and three applied AI to agricultural tweets. Content and data analytics was the most common design (52%), and none of the studies was a randomised trial. Scopus indexed 54% of the eligible AI studies but only 14% of the eligible social media studies. Farmers preferred WhatsApp and familiar tools and created as well as received content, whereas AI was mostly used to analyse farmers' questions and was rarely tested with farmers. The review concludes that the evidence is recent, descriptive and thin on effects, and that future research should test both tools with farmers in the field.

items.title: Society of Nuclear Medicine India Guidelines for Procedure and Reporting of Diuretic Renal Scintigraphy in Adult and Paediatric Patients with Suspected Upper Urinary Tract Obstruction
items.abstract: Diuretic renal scintigraphy (DRS) is the established non-invasive nuclear medicine technique for simultaneously assessing differential renal function (DRF) and upper urinary tract drainage dynamics in patients with suspected obstruction to urinary flow. This Society of Nuclear Medicine India (SNMI) guidelines document aims to provide comprehensive, evidence-based recommendations for the standardised performance, processing, interpretation, and reporting of DRS in both adult and paediatric patients with dilated upper urinary tract, with due consideration of the Indian context. The guidelines address patient preparation, hydration protocols, bladder management, radiopharmaceutical selection (tubular agents such as Tc-99m L,L EC and Tc-99m MAG3 are preferred), furosemide dosing and timing protocols (F−15, F=0, F+20), acquisition parameters, interpretation parameters including semiquantitative metrics such as T½, normalised residual activity (NORA), and DRF, as well as structured reporting and interpretation criteria. Due emphasis is placed on technical quality assurance, recognition of indeterminate and non-diagnostic studies, radiation safety and as low as reasonably achievable (ALARA) principles, and infrastructure requirements applicable to Indian nuclear medicine centres. The limitations inherent to the technique are discussed, and a note is made on future directions (e.g., artificial intelligence-assisted analysis and positron emission tomography (PET) based renography). These guidelines are intended to support nuclear medicine physicians in delivering consistent, high-quality DRS studies that guide timely clinical decision-making and preserve long-term renal function.

items.abstract: Solving new large language model (LLM) and robotic based oncology clinical trial industry problems requires proper publication of protocols, standards, legislation, and funding applications prior to deployment. This paper provides solution sets derived from prior author works for upcoming Physical SI (super intelligence) oncology trials. The publications referenced here require whole implementation, as capabilities differ between state-of-the-art AI models and robots per problem type. Many AI manufacturers’ models have been tested between 2024-2025 in order to discover novel and useful clinical trial applications. These developments include the creation of a patient matching machine learning pipeline, the combination of generated clinical trial meta-analyses to provide new AI insights for indications and cancer drugs, emerging clinical trial simulations, and accelerating the speed and quality of the academic paper creation process. Ultimately, 2026 multi-prompt processes have been optimized to single master prompt systems featured in new trial protocols, drug applications, and funding requests - which feature autonomous AI sub-prompt generation and execution, professional machine readable diagrams, and iterations of full academic paper source code files using a repository-based LLM. Resulting single master prompt-based publications contained high contextual awareness, with a limited number of author corrections required for diagram positioning and paper formatting. Two comprehensive LLM and oncology clinical trial literature reviews conducted in 2025 and 2026 yielded a limited number applications, delayed implementations of new AI models - prompting the oncology trial solutions.

items.title: Sovereign European AI Built on Permissively Licensed Open Models
items.abstract: Abstract This paper examines the conditions under which a European organization can adopt a permissively licensed language model, develop it further within a confidential environment, retain control over its model weights and training materials, and reduce dependence on NVIDIA hardware and other concentrated infrastructure suppliers. The analysis combines a targeted review of model releases and license terms, an assessment of European Union and national legal requirements, a threat-model-based security architecture, and a staged procurement and development roadmap. The study forms part of the broader intellectual and research context of Omegacene, an interdisciplinary project examining the implications of artificial intelligence, technological transformation, and the changing relationship between human and machine agency. Within this context, AI sovereignty is treated not merely as a question of model ownership or infrastructure procurement, but as a problem of institutional control, verifiable accountability, and the capacity to make consequential technological systems independently assessable and governable. The central finding is that model licensing, regulatory compliance, operational security, and supply-chain sovereignty are separate but interdependent dimensions. Apache License 2.0 generally permits confidential modification without an obligation to publish derivative artifacts. This permission does not establish the lawfulness of training data, guarantee freedom from third-party rights, or exempt a downstream organization from applicable AI, data protection, cybersecurity, or procurement law. The European Commission’s compute-based guidance on modifications of general-purpose AI models provides a useful planning indicator, but it does not constitute a statutory exemption or a security threshold. Technical transparency can improve auditability but cannot prove the absence of malicious behavior. Confidential execution, access controls, artifact signing, and model-extraction defenses reduce particular risks without providing absolute protection. Hardware independence is likewise multidimensional: replacing NVIDIA with another supplier does not eliminate dependence on non-European fabrication, memory, interconnects, firmware, or design tools. Advanced fabrication already exists within the EU, but the evidence reviewed does not establish a complete, independently controllable European accelerator supply chain. The paper proposes three complementary model-development tracks, a four-zone security architecture, measurable procurement requirements, corrected compute estimates, and a risk register. Its principal contribution is a framework for making sovereignty claims testable by translating broad aspirations into explicit technical, legal, operational, and supply-chain criteria. In the wider Omegacene.com context, this approach offers a practical basis for evaluating whether control over AI systems is substantive, demonstrable, and resilient, rather than merely asserted through licensing choices or national affiliation. Keywords: digital sovereignty; general-purpose AI; Apache License 2.0; AI Act; confidential model development; model weights; trade secrets; confidential computing; export controls; semiconductor supply chains; EuroHPC; public procurement.

items.title: SpecLLM: LLM-based VNIR spectral interpretation
items.abstract: Abstract Visible and near-infrared (VNIR) spectroscopy identifies materials from characteristic spectral bands, and spectroscopists interpret spectra by features such as peak positions and intensities. Recent machine-learning and foundation models for hyperspectral data are highly effective but return numerical outputs or latent representations rather than such feature-level descriptions. Meanwhile, LLM-based spectral approaches have mostly provided raw numerical sequences. We present a method for making spectroscopic data accessible to large language models (LLMs) through compact, feature-based representations. Instead of supplying full spectra as comma-separated values (CSV), JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), or extensible markup language (XML), the proposed approach extracts summary statistics and discriminative extrema. It serialises them as either natural language or structured JSON. We evaluate prototype-based substance classification in two complementary scenes from an open-access VNIR hyperspectral blood dataset. For the selected models, compact feature representations were substantially more effective than raw numerical encodings, but less effective than a Random Forest operating on raw spectra. The natural-language format provides a human-readable, inspectable serialisation of compact spectral evidence and reduces prompt length compared with full-spectrum encodings. We also compared natural language and JSON feature representations and found them broadly comparable.

items.title: Spin-Transfer Torque MRAM (STT-MRAM) and Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT) In-Memory Computing: Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy, Crossbar Arrays, and Deep Learning Accelerators
items.abstract: The insatiable memory bandwidth demands of deep learning foundation models and edge artificial intelligence are bottlenecked by the Von Neumann bottleneck: the continuous energy-prohibitive shuttling of weights and activations between off-chip dynamic RAM (DRAM) and processor arithmetic logic units (ALUs). Magnetoresistive Random Access Memory (MRAM), anchored by magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) exhibiting Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy (PMA), establishes a non-volatile, radiation-hardened, and virtually wear-out-free memory technology capable of high-density integration alongside sub-5nm CMOS logic. By exploiting Spin-Transfer Torque (STT) and emerging three-terminal SpinOrbit Torque (SOT) switching mechanisms, MRAM enables ultra-fast write speeds (~ns) and zero standby leakage power. Furthermore, integrating MTJ crossbar arrays into non-volatile In-Memory Computing (IMC) architectures allows matrix-vector multiplications (MVM)—the dominant workload in neural network inference—to be executed natively inside memory via Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws with sub-nanosecond latency and massive energy reduction. However, translating spintronic devices into production in-memory computing systems introduces severe physical and circuit bottlenecks: stochastic thermal switching jitter, limited tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) ratios restricting multi-bit precision, IRdrop voltage drops across dense crossbar lines, and write-read disturbance errors. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of STT-MRAM and SOT-MRAM in-memory computing architectures. We formalize spin-transfer torque switching dynamics via the Landau-Lifshitz-GilbertSlonczewski (LLGS) equation, derive crossbar non-volatile dot-product transfer functions, and model stochastic thermal stability factors under PMA scaling. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise SPICE and hardware-in-the-loop testbed evaluating 64Mb STT-MRAM macro arrays and 3-terminal SOT-MRAM neuromorphic inference accelerators across Vision Transformers and ResNet workloads. Our empirical findings demonstrate that our SOT-MRAM in-memory accelerator achieves an energy efficiency of 142.6 Tera-Operations per Second per Watt (TOPS/W)—a 14x improvement over 4nm digital GPU SRAM caches—while sustaining a sub-nanosecond MVM latency and 98.4% image classification accuracy. Finally, we formulate open challenges in ultra-dense 3D vertical MTJ integration, all-spintronic non-volatile spiking logic, and quantum-resistant spintronic PUFs.

items.title: STRATEGIC HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DIGITAL COMMERCE, AND AI-DRIVEN MARKETING: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE
items.abstract: Digital transformation has intensified the need for organizations to align workforce strategy, digital commerce systems, and intelligent marketing capabilities. This comprehensive review examines how strategic human resource management, digital commerce, and AI-driven marketing support sustainable business growth and organizational performance. The review synthesizes literature on digital workforce planning, reskilling, platform-based commerce, marketing automation, predictive analytics, customer personalization, employee engagement, organizational resilience, and ethical governance. The findings indicate that strategic human resource management provides the capability foundation by developing digital skills, adaptive leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous learning. Digital commerce serves as the value-creation and delivery infrastructure through online platforms, fintech integration, omnichannel systems, and network-based business models. AI-driven marketing serves as the customer-intelligence mechanism by enabling segmentation, forecasting, automation, personalization, and real-time engagement. Their coordinated integration can strengthen innovation, productivity, customer experience, revenue generation, and resilience. However, sustainable outcomes depend on reliable data, employee trust, human oversight, privacy protection, algorithmic fairness, and accountable governance. The review proposes an integrated framework linking people, commerce, and marketing capabilities through innovation, efficiency, engagement, and customer value. Future research should empirically test this framework across industries, firm sizes, and national contexts using longitudinal and standardized performance measures. It identifies research priorities concerning human–AI collaboration, digital inclusion, and environmental performance measurement.

items.title: Students' Perceptions on AI Utilization and Regulation: Basis for Developing Guidelines for Responsible Use in Higher Education
items.abstract: In the contemporary era, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become increasingly integrated into education, influencing how students learn, engage, and accomplish academic tasks. This study examined students’ perceptions of AI along two distinct dimensions: utilization and regulation to serve as an evidence-based basis for developing institutional guidelines. Specifically, it addressed four areas of utilization: AI literacy, academic writing support, personalized learning, and student engagement; and two areas of regulation: awareness of AI policies, rules and regulations, and academic integrity and ethical concerns. A descriptive research design was employed, using a survey questionnaire administered to 229 students from the Teacher Education Program at the Polytechnic College of the City of Meycauayan. Data were collected through online and printed forms and analyzed using descriptive statistics, specifically weighted mean, to determine general trends in students’ responses. On utilization, students generally perceived AI as a useful educational tool that enhances learning efficiency, supports academic writing tasks, and enables personalized, self-paced learning. They demonstrated moderate to high AI literacy, with strong awareness of potential misuse and privacy risks, though some reported difficulty learning new AI tools. Usage varied across platforms: Canva, ChatGPT, and Grammarly were the most familiar and widely used, while other tools had limited adoption. On regulation, students expressed strong support for institutional policies, rules, and accountability frameworks. They showed high awareness of ethical standards, data privacy, fairness, and responsible use. yet were less supportive of mandatory disclosure of AI assistance in academic work. Concerns about over-reliance, the absence of clear existing rules, and the urgent need for formal guidance were clearly evident. The study concludes that while AI offers significant educational benefits, comprehensive institutional guidelines on AI utilization and regulation are urgently needed to ensure responsible, ethical, and equitable use. Recommendations include integrating AI literacy training, establishing level-based usage policies, requiring transparency in AI assistance, and upholding academic integrity through clear ethical standards. These findings provide a data-driven foundation for balanced institutional policies that support innovation while maintaining academic integrity and fairness.

items.abstract: Teacher’s Guide to the AI-Driven Classroom Toolkit is a practical resource for building teachers’ capacity to use artificial intelligence responsibly and effectively in teaching and learning. Developed for educators, the toolkit introduces foundational concepts in artificial intelligence, digital literacy, prompt engineering, AI-supported lesson planning, assessment, differentiated instruction, student engagement, and reflective teaching practice. It also presents practical guidance for working in low-resource environments with limited access to devices and reliable internet connectivity. The toolkit discusses responsible and ethical AI use, including accuracy verification, data privacy, academic integrity, bias awareness, fairness, inclusion, transparency, and the continuing importance of teacher judgment and human oversight. It highlights AI as a support tool that can enhance teaching efficiency and learning experiences without replacing the professional, relational, and ethical responsibilities of educators. The resource is intended for teachers, teacher educators, education administrators, professional-development facilitators, researchers, and other stakeholders interested in practical AI integration in schools.

items.title: Teachers' Nonverbal Immediacy and GFP Students' Intrinsic Motivation:An Application of Immediacy Theory
items.abstract: This is a theoretical paper that evaluates the correlation between the nonverbal immediacy behaviors of the teachers and the intrinsic motivation of students undertaking General Foundation Programs (GFP) in tertiary education using the Immediacy Theory by Mehrabian as the main point of analysis. Nonverbal immediacy operationalized in terms of behaviors including eye contact, gestures, facial expressions, vocal variety, and physical proximity has been repeatedly linked with positive affective learning experiences in a variety of educational settings. This paper will use the Immediacy Theory which suggests that communicative behaviors that lead to minimization of psychological distance create relational closeness and positive affect to explain how behaviors can be used to develop intrinsic motivation in GFP students. The GFP context is a special pedagogical context where students who have left secondary and started their higher education often come across linguistic, academic and psychological demands, making teacher immediacy more consequential. The presented paper is a narrative literature review of both empirical and theoretical articles published in 2000-2024 that have been identified by applying a set of preset inclusion and exclusion criteria via a systematic search of ERIC, Google Scholar, and JSTOR databases. The review incorporates the discoveries in the spheres of communication, educational psychology and second-language acquisition to develop a conceptual framework of how teacher nonverbal immediacy is related to increased intrinsic motivation, and the quality of teacher-student relationships is suggested as a critical mediating variable. The paper ends with conclusions about practical implications to GFP instructors, institutional stakeholders, and the future empirical research directions.

items.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into in these aspects of educational environments has initiated more of a paradigm shift in pedagogical structural methodologies, assessment strategies, and the use of fundamental role of educators. This comprehensive review always seems to be examined the current state of teaching competency in the age of AI, focusing here on three pivotal dimensions: teachers' attitudes towards AI, their adaptability of such aspects in utilizing intelligent tools, and their professional commitment in an era of rapid technological disruption-based aspects. Drawing upon a more natured based synthesis of recent literature, we therefore explore how factors such as AI literacy, generative based AI competence, & as also AI-TPACK (Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge) influence here in the successful integration of AI into classrooms everywhere. The review in this aspects highlights that while educators here are increasingly by recognizing the potential of AI to more enhance personalized learning as well as administrative efficiency, there remain in this way to stay neutral significant barriers related to AI anxiety as also, ethical concerns, & most of all a lack of targeted based on professional development. Adaptability is conceptualized not merely as herein technical proficiency, but as a continuous pedagogical evolution requiring robust organizational support-based aspects. Furthermore, professional aspects of commitment in this nature always is analyzed through the lens of shifting teacher identities & the ethical imperative to foster critical thinking and human-centric values based through in AI-augmented learning environments. A prominent table-based data related structure is provided to synthesize the thematic findings, mapping core competencies and against professional development needs. The paper in this manner concludes with actionable recommendations for policymakers, teacher training programs, & future research directions to ensure that educators are adequately equipped here to navigate the complexities of AI in education.

items.title: THE APPLICATION OF DIGITAL IMAGING TECHNOLOGY IN THE UNIVERSITY FINANCIAL REIMBURSEMENT PROCESS: A CASE STUDY OF UNIVERSITY N
items.abstract: Faculty members and students at many newly established universities often find the reimbursement process confusing, and repeated errors end up slowing down the entire procedure. Drawing on the actual situation at University N, this study looks closely at where its financial reimbursement system falls short and proposes a set of concrete measures to improve it, in the hope of offering a workable reference for the digital transformation of reimbursement work at similar institutions. The core idea is to use AI video generation tools to produce short demonstration clips of the reimbursement workflow, and to examine whether artificial intelligence and digital imaging technologies can make university reimbursement more intuitive, more carefully managed, and more intelligent. The findings indicate that these technologies do help: they raise reimbursement efficiency, bring down operating costs, and strengthen the control of compliance risks.

items.title: The Axiology of Arabic Language Education in the Age of Generative AI: Toward an Integrative Framework of Educational Values
items.abstract: The presence of of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Arabic language education raises fundamental questions about educational purposes and values. This qualitative conceptual study, based on a literature review, aims to reconstruct the axiological foundations of Arabic language education by integrating intrinsic, instrumental, and transformative values. The study employs critical philosophical analysis and theoretical synthesis. The findings identify three educational value orientations: linguistic and cultural understanding, communicative competence and social participation, and the development of critical thinking, learner agency, and ethical responsibility. Their integration yields four pedagogical principles: justification of educational purposes, alignment between learning and assessment, source traceability, and human accountability. This study contributes an integrative normative framework for guiding curriculum development, teaching, assessment, and responsible AI governance in Arabic language education.

items.title: The buffering role of exercise enjoyment in the associations among multidimensional psychological stressors, self-focused attention, and generalized social anxiety
items.abstract: Working adults are facing an escalating problem with generalized social anxiety, a public health concern that appears to be compounded by current workplace conditions, especially intense competition and heightened environmental sensitivity. External workplace stressors are known to relate to generalized social anxiety, but the underlying internal cognitive associative patterns and potential buffering factors remain poorly understood. Drawing on the cognitive model of social anxiety and the broaden-and-build theory of positive emotions, this research examined self-focused attention as a mediator and exercise enjoyment as a buffer in the association between multidimensional psychological stressors and generalized social anxiety. This study followed an exploratory-confirmatory design. Study 1 used a custom Python script to conduct Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling across 162,155 online texts. Study 2 surveyed 1,535 white-collar professionals in a cross-sectional design, and the proposed moderated mediation model was tested using the PROCESS macro (Model 4 and Model 59). Preliminary text-mining results supported the ecological validity of the proposed theoretical framework. Multidimensional psychological stressors related significantly and positively to generalized social anxiety ( b = 0.346, 95% CI [0.270, 0.422]); indirect links through self-focused attention arousal ( b = 0.081, 95% CI [0.044, 0.120]) and self-focused attention behavior ( b = 0.064, 95% CI [0.029, 0.104]) were significant as well. Exercise enjoyment exhibited a significant negative moderating role ( b = -0.179, 95% CI [-0.250, -0.108]), and at high levels of exercise enjoyment, neither arousal ( b = 0.001, 95% CI [-0.062, 0.065]) nor behavior ( b = -0.010, 95% CI [-0.076, 0.055]) remained significantly associated with generalized social anxiety. A self-focused attention link appears to statistically connect multidimensional psychological stressors with concurrent generalized social anxiety, and exercise enjoyment seems capable of buffering this internal cognitive association, particularly when physical activity is driven by intrinsic enjoyment rather than mere behavioral compliance. Consequently, workplace physical-activity interventions built around enjoyment, intrinsic motivation, and psychological resource building are recommended as a promising strategic avenue.

items.title: The Himalaya Paradox: Epistemic Collapse of LLM Averageism and Catastrophe-Theoretic Grounding under Extremal Constraints
items.abstract: This technical memorandum exposes a systematic failure mode in autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs): Epistemic Averageism—the pathological tendency to default to unconstrained statistical symmetry, spatial homogeneity, and uncoupled Markovian independence when modeling non-linear, path-dependent physical and geopolitical systems. We document an adversarial stress test (EXP-20261013-EXTREMAL-VS-MEAN) wherein an LLM erroneously calculates the recurring conflict probability of a high-stress geopolitical fault line as an uncoupled independent product (P = (0.2)^2 = 0.04), completely obscuring historical hysteretic strain. To formalize this breakdown, we formulate the Himalaya Paradox: global mean scalar integration (e.g., Earth's mean elevation of 840 m) strips away the singular gradients (e.g., the 8,848 m Himalayan barrier) that strictly govern planetary fluid dynamics, climate morphology, and civilizational topology. By mapping this phenomenon onto René Thom’s cusp catastrophe manifold (Δ = 4u^3 + 27v^2 = 0), we demonstrate that system evolution is governed by extremal singular gradients rather than cross-entropy mean convergence. Finally, we introduce the Teleological Causality Benchmark (TCB) (comprising the "50-meter car wash" and "rain-induced hypothermia" probes) as a minimal adversarial topology proving that token proximity heuristics consistently fail in the presence of physical teleological constraints. This work substantiates the Human-AI Synergy Theory (YQ-HAET) by affirming that the human operator must remain the sovereign source of external negative entropy to anchor probabilistic manifolds to physical reality. *Note: Version 2 updates figure rendering and mathematical typography.*
